primary_topics: Personal testimony delivered at a Bukas Loob sa Diyos (BLD) community gathering, October 18, 1995 -- three weeks after CJP's SC appointment (he 'took his oath only a week ago'); the earliest primary account in the corpus of the JBC seven-rejection narrative
The ten-lepers gospel: only the Samaritan (non-convert) returned to thank Jesus; CJP positions himself and BLD as those who come back to give thanks

The JBC seven-rejection narrative (1992-1994): failed in all seven vacancies; 'many times, I cried and would ask the Lord: How long, O Lord must I bear this frustration and embarrassment of being rejected?'; January 1995 prayer of surrender; July 1995 revival and the two Luke passages; September 20, 1995 miraculous JBC passage

The governing lesson: 'Our God took His time because He wanted me to learn some lessons in humility and in purification. He wanted me to acknowledge my powerlessness. He wanted me to recognize His power over all things.'
sub_topics: Setting: 'it is our intention to tell the Lord, that in BLD, we shall all go back to thank and praise the Lord'
Personal sharing: (1) the validity and effectiveness of the BLD discernment process; (2) the value of faith in obeying God's will after discernment

The appointment: 'I was recently appointed Justice of the Supreme Court of the Philippines. I took my oath only a week ago. Being elevated to the Supreme Court is the highest aspiration and dream of every lawyer. My serious quest began some three years ago.'

Seven rejections (1992-1994): 'seven vacancies... my name was submitted for screening. But in all seven, I failed the test. Many objections were raised against me... Many times, I cried and would ask the Lord: How long, O Lord must I bear this frustration and embarrassment of being rejected?'

Faith anchor: 'In all these instances, I never lost faith in His wisdom and providence. I always took comfort and consolation in Romans 8:28: God makes all things work together for the good of those who love Him and are called according to His purpose.'

January 1995 surrender: 'after seven by-passes, I humbled myself and bowed to what I thought was God's will for me. I uplifted my ambition to God with the prayer: Take, O Lord, all that I am, all that I will ever be. Take my personal ambition, my liberty, my career. Do what You will with them and I will follow whatever it is you want me to do.'

July 1995 revival: a close friend asked him to try again; woke at 1:00 AM July 29, prayed for over two hours; July 30 Sunday gospel (Luke 11: 'Ask and you shall receive, seek and you shall find, knock and the door shall be opened'); 'I perspired coldly and gasped, My Lord, are you asking me to persist in my quest?'

August 6 confirmation: 'gospel was on the transfiguration of our Lord Jesus. From the cloud came a voice which said, This is my Son, my Chosen One. Listen to Him. These three words struck me. And then, I was sure what the Lord wanted me to do.'

September 20 miracle: 'During the JBC meeting on September 20, no one, by some mysterious reason, objected to my name and for the first time in over three years, I passed the screening. A proclaimed miracle! Thereafter, the list of nominees was sent to the President, who called me by phone saying in effect, I am the Lord's instrument. He has chosen you and I therefore appoint you Justice of the Supreme Court.'

Governing lesson: 'Our God took His time because He wanted me to learn some lessons in humility and in purification. He wanted me to acknowledge my powerlessness. He wanted me to recognize His power over all things.'

stances.claim: This October 18, 1995 BLD testimony is the earliest primary account in the corpus of the JBC seven-rejection narrative, delivered while the experience was only eight days old (SC appointment October 10; testimony October 18). All later retellings (SC081, SC130, SD136) draw from this ur-text. The details here are the most immediate and emotionally raw: the specific mention of 'crying,' the precise date (July 29, 1:00 AM), and the President's phone words ('I am the Lord's instrument').
stances.rhetorical_move: earliest-account-as-authoritative: the eight-days-old testimony as the ur-text of the JBC narrative with the most emotionally immediate details
stances.confidence: asserted as the governing origin text

stances.claim: The governing lesson -- 'God wanted me to learn lessons in humility and purification; to acknowledge my powerlessness; to recognize His power over all things' -- is the theological interpretation CJP has consistently given to the seven JBC rejections across all subsequent retellings. This October 1995 statement is the first and most immediate articulation of that interpretation.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered October 18, 1995 at a Bukas Loob sa Diyos (BLD) Covenant Community gathering -- 'I took my oath only a week ago' -- this is the earliest primary account of the JBC seven-rejection narrative in the corpus, delivered eight days after the October 10, 1995 appointment. Using the ten-lepers gospel (only the Samaritan returned to thank Jesus), CJP positions himself and BLD as those who 'go back to thank and praise the Lord.' His sharing on two points: (1) the validity and effectiveness of the BLD discernment process; and (2) the value of faith in obeying God's will. From 1992 to 1994: seven SC vacancies, seven JBC screenings, seven failures. 'Many times, I cried and would ask the Lord: How long, O Lord must I bear this frustration and embarrassment of being rejected?' His faith anchor: Romans 8:28. January 1995: 'I humbled myself and bowed... Take, O Lord, all that I am, all that I will ever be. Take my personal ambition, my liberty, my career. Do what You will with them and I will follow whatever it is you want me to do.' July 1995 revival: a close friend urged him to try again; at 1:00 AM Saturday July 29, he woke and prayed for two hours; Sunday July 30, the Luke 11 gospel ('Ask and you shall receive... knock and the door shall be opened'): 'I perspired coldly and gasped, My Lord, are you asking me to persist in my quest?' August 6 confirmation: the Transfiguration gospel; 'From the cloud came a voice which said, This is my Son, my Chosen One. Listen to Him. These three words struck me.' September 20: 'no one, by some mysterious reason, objected to my name... for the first time in over three years, I passed the screening. A proclaimed miracle! Thereafter, the list of nominees was sent to the President, who called me by phone saying in effect, I am the Lord's instrument. He has chosen you and I therefore appoint you Justice of the Supreme Court.' Governing lesson: 'Our God took His time because He wanted me to learn lessons in humility and in purification. He wanted me to acknowledge my powerlessness. He wanted me to recognize His power over all things.'
